sections.title: What you know
sections.content: In the last lesson you met *No hay nadie que sepa la respuesta*: when a sentence says that something does not exist, the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive. This lesson works through the negative words and adds questions.

sections.title: Negative words before que
sections.content: The word before *que* can be *nadie* "nobody", *nada* "nothing", *ningún* or *ninguna* with a noun "not a single", or *ninguno* on its own. All of them say "there is none", so the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive.

sections.title: Nobody, nothing, not one
rows: No hay nadie que pueda ayudarnos.
There is nobody who can help us.
No hay nada aquí que me guste.
There is nothing here that I like.
No conozco ningún restaurante que abra los lunes.
I don't know any restaurant that opens on Mondays.
No tengo ninguna amiga que viva cerca.
I don't have a single friend who lives nearby.

sections.title: Questions
sections.content: A question asks whether something exists, so the speaker does not know yet: *¿Hay alguien que sepa arreglar esto?* takes the subjunctive. If the speaker is sure that such a person exists, the indicative comes back: *Hay alguien que sabe arreglarlo*.

items.english: Do you know anyone who can cook?

items.spanish: Sí, conozco a alguien que sabe cocinar muy bien.
items.english: Yes, I know someone who cooks very well.

items.spanish: No hay ningún libro aquí que me interese.
items.english: There is no book here that interests me.

items.spanish: ¿Hay algún plomero que pueda venir hoy?
items.english: Is there a plumber who can come today?

sections.content: A negative verb does not always bring the subjunctive: the thing described must be the one that does not exist. *No me gusta la casa que compraste* describes a real house, so it takes the indicative. Compare *No hay ninguna casa que me guste*, where there is no such house.
